title: Multi-Channel AI Messaging Platform
description: A prototype messaging backend that normalizes channel operations behind adapters and moves message work through Redis-backed queues.
thesis: Separate channel-specific delivery from conversation state and asynchronous processing so each boundary can be inspected independently.
problem: Inbound webhooks, channel APIs, user authorization, and background processing cross different trust and failure boundaries.
role: The inspected repository establishes implementation artifacts but does not establish an individual contributor role.
scope: The audited slice covers API registration, channel contracts, queue configuration, authorization middleware, rate limiting, and relational state.
constraints: No customer, delivery-volume, uptime, or deployment claim is made; the audit is limited to local source and schema artifacts.

title: backend/src/app.ts
role: backend/src/app.ts

architecture.label: Fastify API
architecture.relationship: registers webhook, conversation, analytics, handoff, agent, and order routes

architecture.label: Channel adapters
architecture.relationship: define text, template, interactive, and media delivery operations

architecture.label: BullMQ queues
architecture.relationship: configure inbound, outbound, follow-up, and embedding job queues with shared retry policy

architecture.label: PostgreSQL model
architecture.relationship: stores organizations, conversations, messages, roles, and audit records

trust_boundaries.name: Public request to API
trust_boundaries.crossing: Webhook payloads and authenticated API requests enter Fastify routes.

trust_boundaries.name: API to queue
trust_boundaries.crossing: Message work crosses into Redis-backed job queues with retry policy.

security_decisions.risk: Unauthenticated or inactive users reaching protected operations.
security_decisions.control: JWT verification reloads the user and exposes role checks to route handlers.

security_decisions.risk: Burst traffic exhausting global API capacity.
security_decisions.control: The Fastify application registers a global rate-limit plugin with configured limits and windows.

security_decisions.risk: Burst traffic exhausting capacity on routes that use the custom limiter.
security_decisions.control: A Redis counter-based middleware enforces a supplied maximum and time window.

evidence.label: backend/src/app.ts
evidence.title: API composition
evidence.claim: Fastify registers security middleware, health checks, metrics, and domain routes.

evidence.label: backend/src/queue/queue.config.ts
evidence.title: Queue policy
evidence.claim: Four BullMQ queues share bounded retries and exponential backoff.

evidence.label: prisma/schema.prisma
evidence.title: Conversation data model
evidence.claim: The schema defines channel, role, conversation-state, message-status, and audit-log records.

evidence.label: tests/unit/statemachine.test.ts
evidence.title: Conversation state tests
evidence.claim: A local unit-test artifact exercises the conversation state machine.

outcomes.claim: Channel delivery behavior is represented by one adapter contract.
Conversation and message lifecycles have explicit persisted states.

hardening.item: Verify authorization middleware coverage route by route before presenting the API as tenant-isolated.

title: NEPSE Market Intelligence
description: A research system connecting price ingestion, technical indicators, news sentiment, ensemble prediction, backtesting, an API, and a dashboard.
thesis: Keep data provenance, feature construction, model inference, and evaluation visible as separate research stages.
problem: Market data availability, synthetic fallbacks, model dependencies, and test assumptions can materially change what a prediction represents.
role: The inspected repository establishes a local research implementation but does not establish an individual contributor role.
scope: The audited slice covers ingestion, indicator generation, sentiment paths, the three-model ensemble, backtesting, API routes, dashboard code, and the generated report.
constraints: The ingestion path can synthesize historical prices, sentiment can fall back to generated or rule-based data, and no accuracy or return metric is published here.

role: reports/final_report.md

architecture.label: News sentiment

architecture.label: Feature pipeline
architecture.relationship: derives trend, momentum, volatility, and volume indicators

architecture.label: Ensemble predictor
architecture.relationship: combines XGBoost, LSTM, and Transformer probabilities

architecture.label: API and dashboard
architecture.relationship: expose analysis through FastAPI routes and a Streamlit interface

trust_boundaries.name: Price data to research dataset
trust_boundaries.crossing: Downloaded, cached, current, or generated price values enter feature construction.

security_decisions.control: The prediction route normalizes ticker text and bounds its length.

security_decisions.risk: Research consumers mistaking generated history for observed market history.
security_decisions.control: The ingestion code emits an explicit synthetic-data message, but provenance still needs stronger propagation into outputs.

title: Secure Portfolio Platform

thesis: Treat portfolio content, contact submission, administration, and deployment adapters as distinct boundaries with explicit controls and tests.
problem: A public site combines untrusted form input, authenticated administration, mutable content, database variability, and multiple runtime entry points.

title: RunPod Media Orchestrator
description: Prototype RunPod workflow for provisioning GPU compute, transferring prompts, running media jobs, retrieving outputs, and tearing down resources.
thesis: Make the temporary GPU lifecycle explicit from operator confirmation through provisioning, transfer, execution, retrieval, and teardown.
problem: API credentials, generated prompts, remote shell access, output files, and paid compute cross several privilege and data boundaries.
role: The inspected repository establishes an automation implementation but does not establish an individual contributor role.
scope: The audited slice covers channel selection, prompt assembly, operator confirmation, RunPod GraphQL calls, readiness polling, SSH and SFTP transfer, remote execution, SCP retrieval, and termination.
constraints: SSH host keys are accepted automatically, exceptions are handled broadly, and no cost, reliability, audience, or production claim is made.

title: runpod_auto.py
role: runpod_auto.py

architecture.label: Channel selection
architecture.relationship: loads local channel configuration and requires an interactive selection

architecture.label: Prompt assembly
architecture.relationship: generates video, voice, and music prompt components through Gemini with local fallbacks

architecture.label: RunPod GraphQL lifecycle
architecture.relationship: creates a secure-cloud GPU request, polls readiness, and terminates the pod

architecture.label: SSH and SFTP execution
architecture.relationship: uploads prompt data and invokes the remote pipeline

architecture.label: SCP retrieval
architecture.relationship: copies the generated media output back to the operator host

trust_boundaries.name: Operator host to RunPod API
trust_boundaries.crossing: Provisioning and termination requests use an authorization header assembled from configuration.

trust_boundaries.name: Operator host to temporary pod
trust_boundaries.crossing: Prompts, commands, logs, and media files cross SSH-based channels.

security_decisions.risk: Compute provisioning starts without final operator intent.
security_decisions.control: The workflow requires an explicit confirmation before creating a pod.

security_decisions.risk: A readiness timeout leaves temporary compute active.
security_decisions.control: The timeout branch invokes pod termination before returning.

evidence.label: runpod_auto.py
evidence.title: Pod lifecycle
evidence.claim: GraphQL mutations create and terminate the pod around readiness polling and remote execution.

evidence.label: runpod_auto.py
evidence.title: Transfer and execution path
evidence.claim: SFTP writes prompt data, SSH starts the remote pipeline, and SCP retrieves the final media file.

evidence.label: channel_manager.py
evidence.title: Local channel selection
evidence.claim: The command-line manager loads JSON channel configurations and requires an interactive selection.

evidence.label: prompt_generator.py
evidence.title: Prompt generation
evidence.claim: The generator assembles video, voice, and music prompts with explicit local fallbacks.

outcomes.claim: Provisioning, readiness polling, remote execution, retrieval, and teardown are represented in one operator-visible workflow.
The workflow has an explicit cancellation point before compute allocation.

hardening.item: Replace automatic SSH host-key acceptance with pinned or pre-provisioned host verification.
Guarantee pod termination with structured cleanup around every post-provisioning failure path.
